summary: Tahap 1A backend + frontend tested. Backend: 11/13 pytest passed. Core auth (login/logout/me/session/refresh), RBAC (admin-only /users and /security), JWT+Bearer, wrong-password Indonesian error, PATCH user role/active, and self-demotion guard all work. Frontend: login page, wrong-password inline error, password toggle, admin login redirect, theme toggle, logout, unauthenticated redirect, /users table load, staff nav hiding, staff redirect from /users, staff admin-only notice on /security all work. Two functional bugs and three missing data-testid elements found.

critical.issue: Returns 500 (DuplicateKeyError E11000) when creating any user without email after the first one. The unique+sparse index on `email` does NOT ignore explicit null values in MongoDB — only missing fields. Code always inserts `email: None`, so the 2nd user without an email violates the unique index. Fix: (a) drop `email` from the doc when None, OR (b) recreate index as partial: `create_index('email', unique=True, partialFilterExpression={'email': {'$type': 'string'}})`. Repro: log in as admin, POST /api/users with any {username, name, password} without email → 500. Reproduced from both pytest and UI dialog.

Brute-force lockout is effectively bypassable. Identifier uses `request.client.host` which is the internal Kubernetes ingress/pod IP, not the real client. Because the ingress round-robins between backend pods, the identifier alternates (observed 10.219.7.86 vs 10.219.7.96 for the same client), fragmenting the counter so 5-fail lockout never fires from a single real client. Reproduced: 6 sequential wrong-password attempts against the same fake username from the same client never triggered 429. Fix: honor X-Forwarded-For (leftmost, trusted) or key lockout on username only (with a small per-IP+username hybrid), and/or store attempts atomically with $inc.

Submitting the dialog with no email triggers backend 500 (see backend bug); the UI does not surface any error toast to the user — the dialog just closes/stays and the new user is never added. Needs a try/catch with an inline error message or toast for the create-user request.

action_items: Fix POST /api/users 500 by not writing `email: None` (or use partialFilterExpression on the unique email index).
Fix brute-force lockout: derive client IP from X-Forwarded-For (or key attempts on username only) so the counter isn't fragmented across ingress/pod IPs. Use atomic $inc for the counter.
Add `data-testid="dashboard-sidebar"` to sidebar container in DashboardLayout.jsx.
Add `data-testid="session-expiry-timer"` to the session timer element (currently rendering 'Sesi mm:ss').
Surface API errors from Add-User dialog to the user (toast or inline error) instead of failing silently.
Add DialogDescription (or aria-describedby) to DialogContent to fix a11y warning.
critical_code_review_comments: Brute-force identifier trusts `request.client.host` behind a k8s ingress — always resolves to the proxy IP; must use X-Forwarded-For with a trusted-proxy list.
Login counter race: read-then-write update on login_attempts is not atomic; concurrent failed logins can under-count. Use `$inc` with `$setOnInsert`.
`db.users` sparse+unique on email doesn't handle explicit null; either drop the field when None or switch to partialFilterExpression.
`create_user` returns `email` inserted as None even when caller omitted it — inconsistent; strip None before insert.
`session_info` decodes JWT again without wrapping in try/except; a token race where the cookie expires between get_current_user and this decode would 500 instead of 401.
server.py is a single ~400 line file. Fine for Tahap 1A but should be split into routers/auth.py, routers/users.py, security.py, db.py before Tahap 2.
Frontend axios interceptor should refresh on 401 for /auth/me if refresh cookie is present (not verified, code review only).

rca of the issue: Bug 1 (500 on create user): MongoDB's `sparse: true` treats a document as 'not indexed' only when the indexed field is absent. When the code inserts `email: None`, the field is present with value null and gets indexed; the second null violates uniqueness. Fix by omitting the key or using `partialFilterExpression: {email: {$type: 'string'}}`. Bug 2 (lockout not triggering): `request.client.host` returns the immediate socket peer, which — behind Kubernetes ingress — is a rotating proxy pod IP (observed 10.219.7.86 and 10.219.7.96 for the same real client), so `identifier = f'{ip}:{username}'` alternates between multiple keys and neither ever reaches MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS. Real fix: parse the X-Forwarded-For header (leftmost hop) and use that as the client IP, or key lockout on `username` only for the brute-force counter.
